Comment/Citation: Anything other than passive ownership of shares isprohibited for public officials. Officials must transfer the rightof active ownership of the shares or parts of capital they ownto another, unrelated person.(Law on Prevention of the Conflicts of Interests in theExercise of Public Functions, No. 9367,adopted on Apr. 7,2005,published in the Official Journal, No.31, May 11, 2005,art. 22(2) (c),art. 24 (1),art. 38 (1) (c), (i),https:/ /perma.cc/DD3T-A825.)

Persons holding a public office are required to transfer theirstocks and shares to trust management within one monthafter election.(Law of the Republic of Armenia on Public Service, No. ZR-205,adopted as of March 23,2018, last amended on Feb. 7,2020,art.31, para. 10, https://perma.cc/45LH-X8X2(unofficial translation).)
Civil servants must not hold shares for the period ofperforming their duties in the state service. Shares and stocks

owned by civil servants must be transferred to a state-controlled trust.(Law on Public Service in the Republic of Belarus, the Public Service Law, No. 204-3 of 14 June 2003,last amended on July 23, 2019, art. 22, para. 3, https://perma.cc/G6LZ-LWQJ (inRussian).)

Members of Parliament are required to transfer to a trust shares or stocks of a company if they constitute more than0.5% of the company's shares or stocks.(Law on Prevention of Conflicts of Interest, adopted Feb.11,2011, last amended in 2015,art. 16(1),https:/ /perma.cc/B8ST-XQG7.)

Presidential Decree promulgating Law No. 46 of 2014stipulates that members of the Council of Representativesmust not purchase stocks or shares, directly or indirectly, incompanies during their membership in the Council. However, members may increase their capital in a companyor investment project that they owned before theirmembership of the Council of Representatives.(Law No. 46 of 2014,art. 41, al-Jaridah al-Rasmiyah [officialGazette], vol. 23 (annex), 5 June 2014,https:/ /perma.cc/RQ4L-5ERH.)

Legislators are prohibited from owning stock in enterprises they may control in the course of their legislative work. While possession of stocks and shares is allowed by the Rules of Parliamentary Procedure, members of Parliament must not be involved in regular management of their assets.(Law of Georgia on Conflict of Interest and Corruption inPublic Service, No. 982-IS,adopted on Oct. 17,1997, lastamended on Dec. 30, 2021, art.13 para. 12,https:/ /perma.cc/P66A-YKNP, Rules of Procedure of theParliament of Georgia, art.7, paras.2, 3, adopted Dec. 27, 2018, https:/ / perma.cc/W9C8-9738.)

Article 32 of Law 2843/2000 prohibits members of the government, deputy ministers and general or special secretaries of ministries from conducting "stock market transactions [not including] cash sales, and purchasing or

selling shares of mutual funds." Covered persons must notifythe president of the Capital Market Commission of theiraccounts,who will monitor them for violations.Article 13 of Law 3213/2003 extends this prohibition tomembers of the Hellenic Parliament.If a violation is detected under article 32 of Law 2843/2000,the president of the Capital Market Commission must reportthe fact to a special audit committee composed of selectmembers of parliament, judiciary, and high bureaucrats.(Law 2843/2000 on the Modernization of Stock Exchange Transactions, Listing of Investment Companies in Seafaring Shipping on the Athens Stock Exchange and other provisions,art. 32, Government Gazette [E.K.E.D.] 2000,A:219, https:/ /perma.cc/UGK3-VMQR; Law 3213/2003 on theDeclaration and Control of Property Status of Deputies,Public Officials and Employees, Owners of Mass Media andother Categories of Persons,arts. 3A, 13, E.K.E.D.2003, A:309,as amended, https:/ /perma.cc/7RSV-7HGG.)

A person in public life “must refuse or relinquish any ... shareholdings ... which creates or is likely to create a conflictof interest."(Revised Code of Conduct for Public Officers Order 10 of2017 S 4 (3)(c), Guyana Official Gazette Cap. 26:01, Legal Supp. B (June 13, 2017), https:/ / perma.cc/R3DY-95UM.)

A Knesset member (KM) who is a "controlling shareholder"of a corporation (e.g.,holding 50% or more of stock) must sellor lease the shares within six months of commencement of term; a KM "having an interest" in a company (e.g. controlling 5% or more of stock or having the right to appointa director) is required to sell the shares or transfer them to ablind trust until the end of the term.(Ethics Committee Decision 5/18 Regarding Holding ofShares and Prohibition of Serving as a Director in BusinessCompany Ss 5 c, 6 (June 17, 2009), https:/ /perma.cc/8ZLH-YUTE.)

While members of Parliament are allowed to trade shares, stocks and other securities, they cannot acquire more than 5% of voting shares of a commercial organization.(The Law on Combating Corruption of the Republic ofKazakhstan, No. 410-IV LRK, adopted on Nov.18, 2015, art.13.1(2), https:// perma.cc/WS29-UQMX.)

Members of the Parliament "cannot actively exercise his orher ownership rights over shares or parts of capital of acommercial company" and must transfer their securities for management to “another trusted person."(Law on Prevention of Conflict of Interest in the Exercise ofPublic Function of the Republic of Kosovo, No. O4/L-051, inforce since May 12, 2018,art.14, para. 1,art. 16, para. 3,https:/ /perma.cc/NM76-LLJH.)

Members of the legislature and their relatives are prohibited from acquiring and trading shares and stocks of companies working on government contracts during their term in officeand two years thereafter.(Law on Prevention of Conflict of Interest in Activities ofPublic Officials of the Republic of Latvia,Par Interesu KonfliktaNoversanu Valsts Amatpersonu Darbiba, adopted on Apr. 25,2002,last amended on Jan. 21, 2021,art. 10,https:/ / perma.cc/G8PB-Q7S8, https:/ /perma.cc/M7HJ-PJYM (in English).)

Members of Parliament are required to transfer to a trustshares or stocks of companies with the participation of state or municipalities if they own more than 10% of thesesecurities.(Act on Exercising the Mandate of Deputy and Senator, adopted on May 9,1996,last amended in 2006, No.104, item708, Dz. U. 1996, No. 73,art. 34, para. 4,https:/ /perma.cc/ Z9RH-S4FN.)

Ownership of and operations with foreign financialinstruments are prohibited for legislators and their family members. Foreign securities must be eliminated from one's investments before the owner is registered as a candidate forlegislative elections.

(Federal Law No. 13-FZ of July 5,1999,on the Status ofSenators of the Russian Federation and Status of Members ofthe State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the RussianFederation (last amended Dec.21,2021), Sobranie Zakonodatel'stva Rossiiskoi Federatsi (SZ RF) 1999, No. 28, Item 3466 (official publication), https:/ /perma.cc/Q3Q2-EFWB (in Russian).)

Members of the Slovak National Council (legislature) are prohibited during the term of their office from acquiringbearer shares other than by inheritance. Also,within one yearafter leaving office, former legislators cannot be shareholdersof entities if,during their last two years in office, they madedecisions that benefited these entities.(Constitutional Act on the Protection of Public Interest by thePerformance of Offices of Public Officials of the Republic ofSlovakia, No. 357/2004,art. 4(2)e, art. 8(1)c,https:/ / perma.cc/6GX7-6YXP.)

When the aggregate value of all stocks owned by a member of the National Assembly exceeds 30 million won(approximately US$25,000), the member must sell therelevant stocks or conclude a contract on blind trust of stocks.(Public Service Ethics Act, Act No.3520, Dec. 31,1981,asamended by Act No. 17754, Dec.22, 2020,art. 14-4,https://elaw.klri.re.kr/eng_service/lawView.do?hseq=56279&lang=ENG.)

While performing their duties, civil servants must transfertheir shares, stocks,and ownership rights into a trust.(Law On Combating Corruption of the Republic ofTurkmenistan, in force since May 5,2016,art. 11, para. 13,art.12, para. 2, https:/ /perma.cc/9Y89-N9F3 (in Russian).)

The chairperson of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine,his or her first deputy,and the deputy chairperson are required totransfer their securities to a financial institution that willmanage these financial instruments while the owners are inoffice, within one month following the election. Suchcontracts cannot be made with financial institutions wherefamily members of the Verkhovna Rada officials are

employed. Provisions restricting the ownership rights ofregular members of the legislature have not been located.(Law of Ukraine on Prevention Corruption, No. 1700-VII,adopted on Oct.14, 2014, last amended on Nov. 17,2021, art. 36, paras. 1, 3, 4, https:/ /perma.cc/RL7M-8GMD (unoficialtranslation).)
